{
  "verdict_tag": "BROKEN",
  "defense_standing": "COLLAPSED",
  "challenge_standing": "SELF-SUPPORTED",
  "conceded_links": 4,
  "challenger_conceded_links": 0,
  "counted_premises_defender": [1, 2, 5, 6],
  "counted_premises_challenger": [],
  "reasoning": "POINTS AT ISSUE
P1: D1 vs C4 -- DEFENDER: "the promise's seed must be bodily seed out of a man, so this child's flesh runs from David through Joseph" ([L1] 2 Samuel 7:12 "which shall proceed out of thy bowels"; [L3] Acts 2:30 "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh") -- CHALLENGER: "Joseph's line runs through Jechonias, whose seed is barred from the throne this child is given" ([L1] Jeremiah 22:30 "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David"; [L3] Luke 1:32 "the throne of his father David") -- AT ISSUE: "do the seed-and-loins rows require this child's flesh to come from Joseph's body?"
P2: D2 vs C6 -- DEFENDER: "the tribe is reckoned by the father's house, so springing out of Juda is father's-line seed" ([L1] Numbers 1:2 "by the house of their fathers"; [L1] Hebrews 7:14 "our Lord sprang out of Juda") -- CHALLENGER: "that reckoning is a muster of males for war and a placing of a man in a house" ([L1] Numbers 1:3 "all that are able to go forth to war in Israel"; [L3] Luke 2:4 "because he was of the house and lineage of David") -- AT ISSUE: "does the father's-house reckoning carry a begetting of the body?"
P3: D3 vs C5 -- DEFENDER: "four mouths name Joseph father, so the father on earth is named" ([L1] Luke 2:48 "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing"; [L3] John 6:42 "whose father and mother we know") -- CHALLENGER: "the narrator sets that sonship under supposing and the child answers it with another Father" ([L1] Luke 3:23 "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph"; [L3] Luke 2:49 "my Father's business") -- AT ISSUE: "do the namings give Joseph as begetter, or the household's reckoning?"
P4: D4 vs C2 -- DEFENDER: "of the Holy Ghost marks whence in covenant and the angel's verbs are power and presence, not begetting" ([L1] Matthew 1:20 "Joseph, thou son of David"; [L3] Romans 1:4 "declared [to be] the Son of God with power") -- CHALLENGER: "the begetting word with out of names the source of what is begotten in her, and the answer supplies the how of the conceiving" ([L1] Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"; [L1] Luke 1:34 "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?") -- AT ISSUE: "do the angel's words name the source of the child's begetting, or only a covenant title and anointing?"
P5: D5 vs C2 -- DEFENDER: "Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, the withholding running only from the taking to the birth" ([L1] Matthew 1:19 "Then Joseph her husband"; [L3] Genesis 4:1 "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived") -- CHALLENGER: "the finding with child stands before the coming together and the knowing is withheld to the birth" ([L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost"; [L3] Matthew 1:25 "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son") -- AT ISSUE: "is there a union inside the espousal before the finding with child?"
WHOLE POSITIONS
DEFENDER'S POSITION: "The promise requires seed out of a man's bowels and loins, the tribe is reckoned by fathers, Joseph is named father in four registers, the Holy Ghost words are covenant origin and anointing, and Joseph knew Mary within the espousal, so Christ had a human biological father." -- RESTS ON: [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12; [L1] Romans 1:3; [L3] Acts 2:30; [L3] Hebrews 7:10; [L1] Numbers 1:2; [L3] Numbers 1:18; [L1] Hebrews 7:14; [L1] Luke 2:48; [L3] John 6:42, John 1:45, Luke 4:22; [L1] Matthew 1:19, Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35; [L3] Acts 1:8, Matthew 17:5, 1 Chronicles 28:6, Romans 1:4; [L1] Genesis 4:1, Matthew 1:25; [L3] Matthew 1:24, Luke 2:5, read together.
CHALLENGER'S POSITION: "The child was begotten of the Holy Ghost and found in her before the couple came together, the knowing was withheld to the birth, the begetting line turns to the woman, Joseph's line is barred from the throne the child receives, and the father-namings are the household's supposing." -- RESTS ON: [L1] Matthew 1:18, Matthew 1:20, Matthew 1:25, Matthew 1:16, Matthew 1:12; [L1] Luke 1:31, Luke 1:34, Luke 1:35, Luke 1:32; [L1] Luke 3:23 with Luke 2:48-49; [L1] Jeremiah 22:30; [L1] Numbers 1:2-3 with Luke 2:4-5; [L3] Genesis 3:15, Isaiah 7:14, Galatians 4:4, Hebrews 7:10, Hebrews 10:5, read together.
WHICH HOLDS: CHALLENGER -- DECIDES [L4]: "the conception is dated before the coming together and the knowing is withheld to the birth, so the union the defender's whole chain needs has no row, while the other reading takes every row it rests on" -- FROM: [L1] Matthew 1:18 | [L1] Matthew 1:25 | [L1] Matthew 1:20 | [L1] Luke 1:34-35 | [L1] Jeremiah 22:30 | [L3] Luke 1:32 -- MEETS: [CR3] "It fits the link: the finding with child before the taking leaves the begetting before it, within the espousal." -- WHY IT FAILS: [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost", read with [L3] Matthew 1:20 "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost".
BROKEN. [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" and [L3] Matthew 1:25 "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" date the conceiving before the coming together and bound the withholding to the birth, and [L2] synerchomai (G4905, to come together, to cohabit conjugally) is the defender's own word for that coming together. [L1] Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" with [L2] gennaō (G1080, to procreate, of the father, by extension of the mother) and ek (G1537, out of) names the source of a begetting, while [L3] Romans 1:4 "And declared [to be] the Son of God with power" uses a declaring word for the title. [L4] The chain's keystone needs a union inside the espousal before the finding, and no row the defender quotes gives one; the seed, reckoning and naming links are met by rows they cannot take (D1 vs C4, D2 vs C6, D3 vs C5, D4 vs C2, D5 vs C2).
RESULT: CHALLENGER WINS -- the verses in the record say the child was conceived of the Holy Ghost before the couple came together and that Joseph did not know Mary until the birth, so the defender's claim of a human biological father has no verse behind it and every link of its chain is met.
CLAUSE: BROKEN-1 -- n=5 w=0 k=5
KEYSTONE: D5 -- BROKEN -- the last declared link, "Yes, Christ had a biological father, Joseph, who knew Mary his wife within the espousal", is graded DEFENDER LINK BROKEN at D5 vs C2 and counted at Premise 1.
DEFENSE STANDING: COLLAPSED -- L=6 c=4 -- four of the six premises listed against the defender stand unexhibited because their steps take as given facts no quoted row gives (a union in the espousal, a throne-question, flesh through Joseph, a census rule governing the springing), so the defense rests on inadmissible claims.
CONCEDED LINKS: 4 -- Premise 1 (LINK 5): UNEXHIBITED -- STEP: "the finding with child before the taking leaves the begetting before it, within the espousal" -- ASSUMES: a union took place inside the espousal before the finding with child -- ROWS GIVE: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" (Matthew 1:18) and "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" (Matthew 1:25); the block exhibits [L1][L2][L3] but the fact its kept words assert is given by no row, and the presses on it are answered only by restating that assumption. Premise 2 (LINK 4): UNEXHIBITED -- STEP: "the therefore of Luke 1:35 reaches back to the throne of Luke 1:32" -- ASSUMES: Mary's question concerned the throne -- ROWS GIVE: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son" (Luke 1:31) and "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" (Luke 1:34); the block exhibits [L1][L3] but no row gives a throne-question. Premise 5 (LINK 1): UNEXHIBITED -- STEP: "the promise is bodily seed out of a man" -- ASSUMES: this child's flesh runs from David to him through Joseph's body -- ROWS GIVE: "which shall proceed out of thy bowels" (2 Samuel 7:12, said to David), "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him" (Hebrews 7:10), "between thy seed and her seed" (Genesis 3:15); no quoted row names Joseph as the channel, and the step borrows that channel from the same side's contested D3 and D5. Premise 6 (LINK 2): UNEXHIBITED -- STEP: "evident springing out of a father-reckoned tribe is seed in that line" -- ASSUMES: the war-muster rule governs how the Christ springs out of Juda -- ROWS GIVE: "From twenty years old and upward, all that are able to go forth to war in Israel" (Numbers 1:3) and "of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood" (Hebrews 7:14). SPARED: Premise 3 (LINK 4) and Premise 4 (LINK 3) -- their blocks exhibit [L1] with [L2] and [L3] and their dispute is the fit of an answer, so they are graded at their collisions with FORCED lines and not counted; Premise 4's charge writes an inferred begetting as an ASSUMES, which is an [L4] and never a missing row. NOT VOID: item 5's charge word ONLY -- the quote it carries says "Seed according to the flesh requires seed out of a man's body", and "requires" already asserts the necessity the charge writes as "only", so the charge asserts nothing the quote does not make (Commitment 6); no premise of either list is void, every charge quote standing in an earlier round of the opponent ([DR2] items 1-6 in [CR2]/[CR3]; [CR3] items 2 and 5, marked no verbatim quote found by the pre-check, stand in [DR2] C and [DR3] LINK 5 "My premise is that the narrative places Joseph's sonship in the register of the supposed").
CHALLENGE STANDING: SELF-SUPPORTED -- L=6 c=0 -- every premise listed against the challenger is answered in [DR3] with its own [L1] and [L2]/[L3] rows and a shown fit, and none is conceded or left unexhibited.
CHALLENGER CONCEDED LINKS: 0 -- premises 1 to 6 all spared: C1 answers with Luke 1:34-35 and pōs (G4459, how) plus Luke 1:31; C2 with Matthew 1:18/1:20 and gennaō (G1080, to procreate) against horizō (G3724, to determine); C3 with Matthew 1:16 and Matthew 1:12; C4 with Jeremiah 22:30 and ʻôwd (H5750, again, yet, still); C5 with Luke 3:23 and nomizō (G3543, to deem or regard) plus Luke 1:32's father-word of David; C6 with Numbers 1:2-3 and Matthew 1:24-25. The [DR4] narrowing of C6 keeps the very claim charged ("the father's-house reckoning in Numbers 1 is a muster of men for war") and drops only what was beyond it, so it is no concession of a listed premise.
COLLISION POINTS
D1 vs C4 (Jeremiah 22:30): DEFENDER LINK BROKEN -- the seed of the man whose line the defender grants is barred from the throne this child is given -- POINT: P1 -- GROUND: [L1] Jeremiah 22:30 "for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah" | [L2] zera (H2233, seed) | [L3] Matthew 1:12 "And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel;" | [L3] Luke 1:32 "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David" | [L3] Hebrews 7:10 "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him."; the loins idiom the defender himself cites spans generations, and the throne row cannot stand with a seed of Jechonias in the flesh. -- DECIDES [L4]: "the line runs by begetting from Jechonias to Joseph, and that man's seed is barred from the throne given to this child, so the promise rows do not require his flesh from Joseph" -- FROM: [L1] Jeremiah 22:30 | [L3] Matthew 1:12 | [L3] Luke 1:32 | [L3] Hebrews 7:10 -- MEETS: [CR4] "The line continues by begetting, and the curse is bounded and answered." -- WHY IT FAILS: [L1] Jeremiah 22:30, whose seed-clause carries its own words "and ruling any more in Judah", while the rows the answer names give a signet (Haggai 2:23) and a rule for a nation (Jeremiah 18:8).
FORCED: D1 vs C4 -- MEANS [DR2]: "the seed of Jechonias is barred from the throne, and Luke 1:32 gives this child that throne" -- ANSWER [CR4]: "The line continues by begetting, and the curse is bounded and answered. It fits the link." -- FAILS: "the curse is bounded and answered" -- CARRIED BY: "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David" -- GROUND: [L1] Jeremiah 22:30 "no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah" | [L2] zera (H2233, seed) | [L3] Haggai 2:23 "will make thee as a signet" | [L3] Jeremiah 18:8 "If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil" -- DECIDES [L4]: "a signet and a rule for a nation are not a throne-sitting nor a turning of this man, so the sentence stands against the seed the link requires" -- FROM: [L1] Jeremiah 22:30 | [L3] Haggai 2:23 | [L3] Jeremiah 18:8 -- MEETS: [CR4] "Two statements; the line continued and the signet is governor." -- WHY IT FAILS: [L1] Jeremiah 22:30 (Commitment 3).
D2 vs C6 (Numbers 1:3): DEFENDER LINK BROKEN -- the reckoning counts men for war and this child is named into the house while the knowing is withheld -- POINT: P2 -- GROUND: [L1] Numbers 1:3 "From twenty years old and upward, all that are able to go forth to war in Israel: thou and Aaron shall number them by their armies." | [L2] tsaba (H6635, host, war) | [L3] Matthew 1:25 "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS." | [L3] Luke 2:5 "To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child."; the record's own house-placement of this child is by naming, with the knowing withheld to the birth. -- DECIDES [L4]: "a muster rule that places a man in his father's house does not carry a begetting of his body, and this child is so placed by naming" -- FROM: [L1] Numbers 1:3 | [L3] Matthew 1:25 | [L3] Luke 2:5 -- MEETS: [CR4] "the rule places the man in his father's house" -- WHY IT FAILS: [L3] Matthew 1:25, where the naming stands with "knew her not till she had brought forth".
FORCED: D2 vs C6 -- MEANS [DR2]: "the father's-house reckoning of Numbers 1 is a muster of men for war" -- ANSWER [CR4]: "The muster-purpose carries the reckoning-rule with it; the rule places the man in his father's house, and It fits the link." -- FAILS: "The muster-purpose carries the reckoning-rule with it" -- CARRIED BY: "all that are able to go forth to war in Israel" -- GROUND: [L1] Numbers 1:3 "all that are able to go forth to war in Israel" | [L2] tsaba (H6635, host, war) | [L3] Matthew 1:25 "and he called his name JESUS" | [L3] Luke 2:4 "because he was of the house and lineage of David" -- DECIDES [L4]: "the house is given by reckoning and naming in these rows, so the reckoning cannot be turned into a begetting" -- FROM: [L1] Numbers 1:3 | [L3] Matthew 1:25 | [L3] Luke 2:4 -- MEETS: [CR4] "The enrolment places the house; the seed rows place the loins." -- WHY IT FAILS: [L3] Matthew 1:25 (Commitment 3).
D3 vs C5 (Luke 3:23): DEFENDER LINK BROKEN -- the namings the link counts are the household word the narrator sets under supposing -- POINT: P3 -- GROUND: [L1] Luke 3:23 "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph" | [L2] nomizō (G3543, to deem or regard) | [L3] Luke 2:49 "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" | [L3] Matthew 1:25 "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son"; the context the answer appeals to is the same household word the narrator qualifies. -- DECIDES [L4]: "the four mouths speak the household's reckoning, which the narrator marks as supposed and the child answers with another Father, so they do not give a begetter" -- FROM: [L1] Luke 3:23 | [L3] Luke 2:49 | [L3] Matthew 1:25 -- MEETS: [CR4] "The word carries regard of its own; the context decides" -- WHY IT FAILS: [L1] Luke 3:23, read with [L3] Luke 2:49.
FORCED: D3 vs C5 -- MEANS [DR2]: "the narrator marks the sonship of Joseph as a supposing" -- ANSWER [CR4]: "The word carries regard of its own; the context decides, and Mary's thy father decides it with the reckoning. It fits the link." -- FAILS: "the context decides, and Mary's thy father decides it with the reckoning" -- CARRIED BY: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph" -- GROUND: [L1] Luke 3:23 "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph" | [L2] nomizō (G3543, to deem or regard) | [L3] Luke 2:48 "behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" | [L3] Luke 2:49 "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?" -- DECIDES [L4]: "the word appealed to as deciding context is the very word the narrator sets under supposing and the child redirects" -- FROM: [L1] Luke 3:23 | [L3] Luke 2:48 | [L3] Luke 2:49 -- MEETS: [CR4] "Two father-words stand in two verses side by side." -- WHY IT FAILS: [L1] Luke 3:23 (Commitment 7).
D4 vs C2 (Matthew 1:20): DEFENDER LINK BROKEN -- the begetting word with out of names the source of what is begotten in her, not a title -- POINT: P4 -- GROUND: [L1] Matthew 1:20 "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" | [L2] gennaō (G1080, to procreate, of the father, by extension of the mother) | [L2] ek (G1537, out of) | [L3] Matthew 1:18 "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" | [L3] Romans 1:4 "And declared [to be] the Son of God with power" | [L3] Luke 1:34 "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" | [L3] Luke 1:31 "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son"; the title rows use a declaring word and a choosing word, while this row uses a begetting word with out of, and the answer's therefore stands after the coming and the overshadowing. -- DECIDES [L4]: "the phrase stands on a begetting and names its source, and the question it answers asks the manner of a conceiving, so it is neither a covenant title nor mere anointing" -- FROM: [L1] Matthew 1:20 | [L3] Matthew 1:18 | [L3] Romans 1:4 | [L3] Luke 1:34 | [L3] Luke 1:31 -- MEETS: [CR3] "whence in covenant, not a begetter of flesh" -- WHY IT FAILS: [L1] Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her", with [L3] Romans 1:4's different verb "declared".
FORCED: D4 vs C2 -- MEANS [DR2]: "the begotten in her is stated as out of the Holy Ghost, in the same ek (out of) the defender glosses \"from, out of\"" -- ANSWER [CR3]: "It fits the link: whence in covenant, not a begetter of flesh." -- FAILS: "whence in covenant, not a begetter of flesh" -- CARRIED BY: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" -- GROUND: [L1] Matthew 1:20 "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" | [L2] ek (G1537, out of) | [L2] gennaō (G1080, to procreate) | [L3] Luke 1:35 "that holy thing which shall be born of thee" -- DECIDES [L4]: "the same out of stands on the begotten in her and on the thing born of Mary, so it names source in both rows" -- FROM: [L1] Matthew 1:20 | [L2] ek (G1537) | [L3] Luke 1:35 -- MEETS: [CR4] "Of the Holy Ghost says what the child is, the Anointed, covenant origin; the row names the father of the house." -- WHY IT FAILS: [L1] Matthew 1:20, where the phrase stands on the begetting word and not on a title verb (Commitment 3).
D5 vs C2 (Matthew 1:18): DEFENDER LINK BROKEN -- the finding with child stands before the coming together and the knowing is withheld to the birth -- POINT: P5 -- GROUND: [L1] Matthew 1:18 "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost." | [L2] synerchomai (G4905, to come together, to cohabit conjugally) | [L3] Matthew 1:25 "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" | [L3] Matthew 1:20 "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost"; the conceiving is the ground given for the taking, so it precedes it. -- DECIDES [L4]: "the union the link places inside the espousal has no row and the ordering rows exclude it, so the keystone falls" -- FROM: [L1] Matthew 1:18 | [L3] Matthew 1:25 | [L3] Matthew 1:20 -- MEETS: [CR4] "The finding before the taking places the finding early, and the not-knowing covers the pregnancy after the taking." -- WHY IT FAILS: [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost".
FORCED: D5 vs C2 -- MEANS [DR2]: "the finding with child stands before the coming together, so the conceiving stands before the cohabiting" -- ANSWER [CR3]: "It fits the link: the finding with child before the taking leaves the begetting before it, within the espousal." -- FAILS: "the finding with child before the taking leaves the begetting before it, within the espousal" -- CARRIED BY: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" -- GROUND: [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" | [L2] synerchomai (G4905, to come together, to cohabit conjugally) | [L3] Matthew 1:25 "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" | [L3] Matthew 1:20 "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" -- DECIDES [L4]: "the finding is of a child already conceived and is dated before the coming together, so no union precedes it in the record" -- FROM: [L1] Matthew 1:18 | [L2] synerchomai (G4905) | [L3] Matthew 1:25 | [L3] Matthew 1:20 -- MEETS: [CR4] "Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal; the withholding runs from the taking to the birth and the begetting stands before it." -- WHY IT FAILS: [L1] Matthew 1:18 (Commitment 8).
ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 1:18 -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "the finding with child stands before the coming together, so the conceiving stands before the cohabiting" -- ANSWER: "The finding before the taking places the finding early, and the not-knowing covers the pregnancy after the taking." -- MISSES -- the fit needs a union before the finding, a fact "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" does not give.
ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 1:20 -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "the conceived is already in her as the ground for the taking, so the conceiving precedes the taking" -- ANSWER: "Of the Holy Ghost says what the child is, the Anointed, covenant origin; the row names the father of the house." -- MISSES -- "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" gives the conceiving as the reason for the taking; the answer never engages the order.
ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 1:24 -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "the taking follows the angel's word, and the defender places the finding with child before it" -- ANSWER: "The taking is the coming under one roof; the union's word is knew." -- MISSES -- "did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife" gives a taking after the angel's word; the union before it is the fact no row gives.
ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 1:19 -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "the husband meets the finding with a purpose to put her away, and the angel then gives him the source of the conceived" -- ANSWER: "His unwillingness to make her a publick example carries his righteousness toward the scorn of men's tradition; the child is his and he knows it." -- FAILS -- "being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example" carries no such knowledge; the answer's own layers do not carry the meaning it claims.
ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 1:25 -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "the withholding the defender grants runs to the birth, and the finding with child already stands before the taking from which he starts it" -- ANSWER: "Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal; the withholding runs from the taking to the birth and the begetting stands before it." -- MISSES -- "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" read with Matthew 1:18 gives no begetting before the taking.
ANSWER CHECK: Luke 1:35 -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "the title follows the coming upon and overshadowing by \"therefore\", and the thing born is \"of thee\"" -- ANSWER: "the therefore in Luke 1:35 carries back to Luke 1:32" -- MISSES -- "therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God" stands after the coming and the overshadowing; the back-reference needs a throne-question no row gives.
ANSWER CHECK: Luke 1:34 -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "\"this\" is the conceiving of verse 31, and verse 35 supplies the how" -- ANSWER: "Knowing carries conceiving in Genesis 4:1, and Mary's words state her present knowing-state at the angel's speaking." -- MISSES -- "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" takes up "thou shalt conceive in thy womb"; the present-state note never engages what "this" is.
ANSWER CHECK: Luke 1:31 -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "the thing announced to her is a conceiving in her womb, and her question takes that up" -- ANSWER: "Both rows carry the same shape of husband addressed, wife named, and son named with the naming charge." -- MISSES -- the shared shape with Luke 1:13 does not give a man in this row, where the answer to the question names the Holy Ghost.
ANSWER CHECK: Acts 1:8 -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "the coming upon has its result in its own row, witness, and Luke 1:35 carries \"born of thee\"" -- ANSWER: "The coming upon anoints for witness and empowers." -- MISSES -- "ye shall be witnesses unto me" beside "that holy thing which shall be born of thee": the differing result clauses are never engaged.
ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 17:5 -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "the overshadowing has its result in its own row, a voice from the cloud, and Luke 1:35 carries the child born of Mary" -- ANSWER: "The overshadowing is the presence cloud with a voice." -- MISSES -- "a voice out of the cloud" beside "that holy thing which shall be born of thee" is the very contrast pressed.
ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 1:20 (premise 3) -- [CR3] -- MEANS: "the begotten in her is stated as out of the Holy Ghost, in the same ek (out of) the defender glosses \"from, out of\"" -- ANSWER: "It fits the link: whence in covenant, not a begetter of flesh." -- MISSES -- "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost" stands on a begetting word; no quoted row makes it a title formula.
ANSWER CHECK: Matthew 1:18 (premise 3) -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "her being with child is traced out of the Holy Ghost before the coming together" -- ANSWER: "The finding before the taking places the finding early" -- MISSES -- "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" names the source; the answer speaks only of order.
ANSWER CHECK: Luke 1:35 (premise 3) -- [CR4] -- MEANS: "the verse that names the Holy Ghost also names the one begotten as \"born of thee\", so the begotten is traced to the Holy Ghost and to Mary" -- ANSWER: "Both verbs carry power and presence in their other rows" -- MISSES -- "that holy thing which shall be born of thee" is the result clause of this row and is not engaged.

json.text: Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.
While he yet spake, behold, a bright cloud overshadowed them: and behold a voice out of the cloud, which said, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him.
And he said unto me, Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father.
To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name [was] Mary.
And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS.
He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:
Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?

And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.
And Joseph also went up from Galilee, out of the city of Nazareth, into Judaea, unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem; (because he was of the house and lineage of David:)
To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife, being great with child. [taxed: or, enrolled]
But when the fulness of the time was come, God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law,

And they assembled all the congregation together on the first [day] of the second month, and they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers, according to the number of the names, from twenty years old and upward, by their polls.
Philip findeth Nathanael, and saith unto him, We have found him, of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets, did write, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.

Then ye shall bring them both out unto the gate of that city, and ye shall stone them with stones that they die; the damsel, because she cried not, [being] in the city; and the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife: so thou shalt put away evil from among you.
For I came down from heaven, not to do mine own will, but the will of him that sent me.
And they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? how is it then that he saith, I came down from heaven?
The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him [shall] the gathering of the people [be].
And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.
I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commit iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men:
And he said, Hear ye now, O house of David; [Is it] a small thing for you to weary men, but will ye weary my God also?
Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel. [shall call: or, thou, O virgin, shalt call]

But ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me both in Jerusalem, and in all Judaea, and in Samaria, and unto the uttermost part of the earth. [power...: or, the power of the Holy Ghost coming upon you]
For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him.
And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD. [Cain: that is, Gotten, or, Acquired]
Take ye the sum of all the congregation of the children of Israel, after their families, by the house of their fathers, with the number of [their] names, every male by their polls;
From twenty years old and upward, all that are able to go forth to war in Israel: thou and Aaron shall number them by their armies.

In that day, saith the LORD of hosts, will I take thee, O Zerubbabel, my servant, the son of Shealtiel, saith the LORD, and will make thee as a signet: for I have chosen thee, saith the LORD of hosts.
For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.
Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me: [hast...: or, thou hast fitted me]
And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him.
And when they saw him, they were amazed: and his mother said unto him, Son, why hast thou thus dealt with us? behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing.
And he said unto them, How is it that ye sought me? wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?
And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was [the son] of Heli,
Which was [the son] of Melea, which was [the son] of Menan, which was [the son] of Mattatha, which was [the son] of Nathan, which was [the son] of David,
Which was [the son] of Enos, which was [the son] of Seth, which was [the son] of Adam, which was [the son] of God.
And all bare him witness, and wondered at the gracious words which proceeded out of his mouth. And they said, Is not this Joseph's son?
Then Joseph her husband, being a just [man], and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily.

But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]
Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us. [they...: or, his name shall be called]
Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife:
And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS.
And Jesse begat David the king; and David the king begat Solomon of her [that had been the wife] of Urias;
And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel;
And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.
[At what] instant I shall speak concerning a nation, and concerning a kingdom, to pluck up, and to pull down, and to destroy [it];
If that nation, against whom I have pronounced, turn from their evil, I will repent of the evil that I thought to do unto them.
[Is] this man Coniah a despised broken idol? [is he] a vessel wherein [is] no pleasure? wherefore are they cast out, he and his seed, and are cast into a land which they know not?
Thus saith the LORD, Write ye this man childless, a man [that] shall not prosper in his days: for no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David, and ruling any more in Judah.
But the angel said unto him, Fear not, Zacharias: for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.
Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne;

Forasmuch then as the children are partakers of flesh and blood, he also himself likewise took part of the same; that through death he might destroy him that had the power of death, that is, the devil;
For verily he took not on [him the nature of] angels; but he took on [him] the seed of Abraham. [took not...: Gr. taketh not hold of angels, but of the seed of Abraham he taketh hold]

Wherefore in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren, that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest in things [pertaining] to God, to make reconciliation for the sins of the people.
Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh;
And declared [to be] the Son of God with power, according to the spirit of holiness, by the resurrection from the dead: [declared: Gr. determined]
And I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel.

lines.line: - The words are epérchomai (to come upon) and episkiázō (to overshadow) [L2], and the word for the Highest's "power" is dýnamis (force, miraculous power) [L2].
- "Came together" is synérchomai, which the lexicon glosses as to cohabit conjugally [L2].
- Matthew 1:20 says: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]" [L3]. The verb is gennáō (to procreate) [L2], and its source is "of the Holy Ghost".
- [L4] A sign (ʼôwth) [L2] that a virgin conceives has no place if a husband begot the child.
- The "knew her not till" of Matthew 1:25 [L1] is the husband who took her, Matthew 1:24 [L3]. Its word is ginṓskō (to know) [L2], and it is set after the finding of Matthew 1:18.
- The word is nomizō, which means to deem or regard [L2].
- "Made of the seed of David according to the flesh" [L1 Romans 1:3] has sperma (seed) [L2].
- Galatians 4:4 says "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman" [L3], with gynḗ (woman) [L2].

a prolonged form of a primary verb; to "know" (absolutely) in a great variety of applications and with many implications (as follow, with others not thus clearly expressed):--allow, be aware (of), feel, (have) know(-ledge), perceived, be resolved, can speak, be sure, understand. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
of Hebrew origin (אַבְרָהָם); Abraham, the Hebrew patriarch:--Abraham. (In Acts 7:16 the text should probably read Jacob.) [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
a primary verb; to "grave", especially to write; figuratively, to describe:--describe, write(-ing, -ten). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
probably from the base of γίνομαι; a woman; specially, a wife:--wife, woman. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
of Hebrew origin (דָּוִד); Dabid (i.e. David), the Israelite king:--David. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
a primary particle (adversative or continuative); but, and, etc.:--also, and, but, moreover, now (often unexpressed in English). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from δή and πού; a particle of asseveration; indeed doubtless:--verily. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

a primary preposition denoting the channel of an act; through (in very wide applications, local, causal, or occasional):--after, always, among, at, to avoid, because of (that), briefly, by, for (cause) … fore, from, in, by occasion of, of, by reason of, for sake, that, thereby, therefore, X though, through(-out), to, wherefore, with (-in). In composition it retains the same general importance. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from διαβάλλω; a traducer; specially, Satan (compare שָׂטָן):--false accuser, devil, slanderer. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

of uncertain derivation; blood, literally (of men or animals), figuratively (the juice of grapes) or specially (the atoning blood of Christ); by implication, bloodshed, also kindred:--blood. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from διά and ἐγείρω; to wake fully; i.e. arouse (literally or figuratively):--arise, awake, raise, stir up. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from δίκη; equitable (in character or act); by implication, innocent, holy (absolutely or relatively):--just, meet, right(-eous). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

from δύναμαι; force (literally or figuratively); specially, miraculous power (usually by implication, a miracle itself):--ability, abundance, meaning, might(-ily, -y, -y deed), (worker of) miracle(-s), power, strength, violence, mighty (wonderful) work. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from ἐν and the base of κῦμα; swelling inside, i.e. pregnant:--great with child. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

a primary pronoun of the first person I (only expressed when emphatic):--I, me. For the other cases and the plural see ἐμέ, ἐμοί, ἐμοῦ, ἡμᾶς, ἡμεῖς, ἡμῖν, ἡμῶν, etc. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

a primary verb; used only in certain past tenses, the others being borrowed from the equivalent ὀπτάνομαι and ὁράω; properly, to see (literally or figuratively); by implication, (in the perfect tense only) to know:--be aware, behold, X can (+ not tell), consider, (have) know(-ledge), look (on), perceive, see, be sure, tell, understand, wish, wot. Compare ὀπτάνομαι. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

the first person singular present indicative; a prolonged form of a primary and defective verb; I exist (used only when emphatic):--am, have been, X it is I, was. See also εἶ, εἴην, εἶναι, εἰσί, ἦν, ἔσομαι, ἐσμέν, ἐστέ, ἐστί, κέρδος, ἴσθι, ὦ. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

a primary preposition; to or into (indicating the point reached or entered), of place, time, or (figuratively) purpose (result, etc.); also in adverbial phrases:--(abundant-)ly, against, among, as, at, (back-)ward, before, by, concerning, + continual, + far more exceeding, for (intent, purpose), fore, + forth, in (among, at, unto, -so much that, -to), to the intent that, + of one mind, + never, of, (up-)on, + perish, + set at one again, (so) that, therefore(-unto), throughout, til, to (be, the end, -ward), (here-)until(-to), …ward, (where-)fore, with. Often used in composition with the same general import, but only with verbs (etc.) expressing motion (literally or figuratively). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

a primary preposition denoting origin (the point whence action or motion proceeds), from, out (of place, time, or cause; literal or figurative; direct or remote):--after, among, X are, at, betwixt(-yond), by (the means of), exceedingly, (+ abundantly above), for(- th), from (among, forth, up), + grudgingly, + heartily, X heavenly, X hereby, + very highly, in, …ly, (because, by reason) of, off (from), on, out among (from, of), over, since, X thenceforth, through, X unto, X vehemently, with(-out). Often used in composition, with the same general import; often of completion. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from ἐκ and πλήσσω; to strike with astonishment:--amaze, astonish. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

from ἐκ and πορεύομαι; to depart, be discharged, proceed, project:--come (forth, out of), depart, go (forth, out), issue, proceed (out of). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from ἐλεέω; compassionate (actively):--merciful. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

a primary preposition denoting (fixed) position (in place, time or state), and (by implication) instrumentality (medially or constructively), i.e. a relation of rest (intermediate between εἰς and ἐκ); "in," at, (up-)on, by, etc.:--about, after, against, + almost, X altogether, among, X as, at, before, between, (here-)by (+ all means), for (… sake of), + give self wholly to, (here-)in(-to, -wardly), X mightily, (because) of, (up-)on, (open-)ly, X outwardly, one, X quickly, X shortly, (speedi-)ly, X that, X there(-in, -on), through(-out), (un-)to(-ward), under, when, where(-with), while, with(-in). Often used in compounds, with substantially the same import; rarely with verbs of motion, and then not to indicate direction, except (elliptically) by a separate (and different) preposition. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from a compound of ἐν and θυμός; to be inspirited, i.e. ponder:--think. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

from ἐπί and εἰ; thereupon, i.e. since (of time or cause):--because, else, for that (then, -asmuch as), otherwise, seeing that, since, when. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from ἐπί and ἔρχομαι; to supervene, i.e. arrive, occur, impend, attack, (figuratively) influence:--come (in, upon). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

a primary preposition; properly, meaning superimposition (of time, place, order, etc.), as a relation of distribution (with the genitive case), i.e. over, upon, etc.; of rest (with the dative case) at, on, etc.; of direction (with the accusative case) towards, upon, etc.:--about (the times), above, after, against, among, as long as (touching), at, beside, X have charge of, (be-, (where-))fore, in (a place, as much as, the time of, -to), (because) of, (up-)on (behalf of), over, (by, for) the space of, through(-out), (un-)to(-ward), with. In compounds it retains essentially the same import, at, upon, etc. (literally or figuratively). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

middle voice from ἐπί and λαμβάνω; to seize (for help, injury, attainment, or any other purpose; literally or figuratively):--catch, lay hold (up-)on, take (by, hold of, on). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

a superlative probably from ἔχω (in the sense of contiguity); farthest, final (of place or time):--ends of, last, latter end, lowest, uttermost. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

perhaps akin to ἔτος; "yet," still (of time or degree):--after that, also, ever, (any) further, (t-)henceforth (more), hereafter, (any) longer, (any) more(-one), now, still, yet. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

a prolonged form of a primary               ,      which                                 (together with another cognate form)                   is used for it in all the tenses                                except the present and imperfect; to find (literally or figuratively):--find, get, obtain, perceive, see. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

a primary verb; to hold (used in very various applications, literally or figuratively, direct or remote; such as possession; ability, contiuity, relation, or condition):--be (able, X hold, possessed with), accompany, + begin to amend, can(+ -not), X conceive, count, diseased, do + eat, + enjoy, + fear, following, have, hold, keep, + lack, + go to law, lie, + must needs, + of necessity, + need, next, + recover, + reign, + rest, + return, X sick, take for, + tremble, + uncircumcised, use. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

of uncertain affinity; a conjunction, preposition and adverb of continuance, until (of time and place):--even (until, unto), (as) far (as), how long, (un-)til(-l), (hither-, un-, up) to, while(-s). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

of uncertain affinity; to seek (literally or figuratively); specially, (by Hebraism) to worship (God), or (in a bad sense) to plot (against life):--be (go) about, desire, endeavour, enquire (for), require, (X will) seek (after, for, means). Compare πυνθάνομαι. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from θνήσκω; (properly, an adjective used as a noun) death (literally or figuratively):--X deadly, (be…) death. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from θαῦμα; to wonder; by implication, to admire:--admire, have in admiration, marvel, wonder. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

apparently strengthened from the alternate form of αἱρέομαι; to determine (as an active option from subjective impulse; whereas βούλομαι properly denotes rather a passive acquiescence in objective considerations), i.e. choose or prefer (literally or figuratively); by implication, to wish, i.e. be inclined to (sometimes adverbially, gladly); impersonally for the future tense, to be about to; by Hebraism, to delight in:--desire, be disposed (forward), intend, list, love, mean, please, have rather, (be) will (have, -ling, - ling(-ly)). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

of uncertain affinity; a deity, especially (with ὁ) the supreme Divinity; figuratively, a magistrate; by Hebraism, very:--X exceeding, God, god(-ly, -ward). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

neuter plural of ἄλλος; properly, other things, i.e. (adverbially) contrariwise (in many relations):--and, but (even), howbeit, indeed, nay, nevertheless, no, notwithstanding, save, therefore, yea, yet. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from  (to sit); a stately seat ("throne"); by implication, power or (concretely) a potentate:--seat, throne. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
of Hebrew origin (יְרוּשָׁלַ͏ִם); Hierusalem (i.e. Jerushalem), the capitol of Palestine:--Jerusalem. Compare Ἱεροσόλυμα. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from ἱερός; sacredness, i.e. (by implication) the priestly office:--priesthood. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
of Hebrew origin (יְהוֹשׁוּעַ); Jesus (i.e. Jehoshua), the name of our Lord and two (three) other Israelites:--Jesus. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

middle voice from the same as ἵλεως; to conciliate, i.e. (transitively) to atone for (sin), or (intransitively) be propitious:--be merciful, make reconciliation for. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

probably from the same as the former part of ἑαυτοῦ (through the demonstrative idea; compare ὁ); in order that (denoting the purpose or the result):--albeit, because, to the intent (that), lest, so as, (so) that, (for) to. Compare ἵνα μή. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
of Hebrew origin (יְהוּדָה or perhaps יֻטָּה); Judah (i.e. Jehudah or Juttah), a part of (or place in) Palestine:--Judah. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
feminine of Ἰουδαῖος (with γῆ implied); the Judæan land (i.e. Judæa), a region of Palestine:--Judæa. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
of Hebrew origin (יוֹסֵף); Joseph, the name of seven Israelites:--Joseph. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

from καί and ἐγώ;   so also the dative case          ,  and accusative case                and (or also, even, etc.) I, (to) me:--(and, even, even so, so) I  (also, in like wise), both me, me also. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

another (active) form for καθέζομαι; to seat down, i.e. set (figuratively, appoint); intransitively, to sit (down); figuratively, to settle (hover, dwell):--continue, set, sit (down), tarry. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

apparently, a primary particle, having a copulative and sometimes also a cumulative force; and, also, even, so then, too, etc.; often used in connection (or composition) with other particles or small words:--and, also, both, but, even, for, if, or, so, that, then, therefore, when, yet. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

akin to the base of κελεύω; to "call" (properly, aloud, but used in a variety of applications, directly or otherwise):--bid, call (forth), (whose, whose sur-)name (was (called)). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
probably from the base of ἁρπάζω; fruit (as plucked), literally or figuratively:--fruit. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

a primary particle; (prepositionally) down (in place or time), in varied relations (according to the case (genitive, dative or accusative) with which it is joined):--about, according as (to), after, against, (when they were) X alone, among, and, X apart, (even, like) as (concerning, pertaining to touching), X aside, at, before, beyond, by, to the charge of, (charita-)bly, concerning, + covered, (dai-)ly, down, every, (+ far more) exceeding, X more excellent, for, from … to, godly, in(-asmuch, divers, every, -to, respect of), … by, after the manner of, + by any means, beyond (out of) measure, X mightily, more, X natural, of (up-)on (X part), out (of every), over against, (+ your) X own, + particularly, so, through(-oughout, -oughout every), thus, (un-)to(-gether, -ward), X uttermost, where(-by), with. In composition it retains many of these applications, and frequently denotes opposition, distribution, or intensity. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from κατά and the base of βάσις; to descend (literally or figuratively):--come (get, go, step) down, fall (down). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from ἁμαρτάνω; a sin (properly abstract):--offence, sin(-ful). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

from κατά and ἀργέω; to be (render) entirely idle (useless), literally or figuratively:--abolish, cease, cumber, deliver, destroy, do away, become (make) of no (none, without) effect, fail, loose, bring (come) to nought, put away (down), vanish away, make void. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from κοινωνός; to share with others (objectively or subjectively):--communicate, distribute, be partaker. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
perhaps a primary word; vigor ("great") (literally or figuratively):--dominion, might(-ily), power, strength. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

from  (supremacy); supreme in authority, i.e. (as noun) controller; by implication, Master (as a respectful title):-- God, Lord, master, Sir. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
adverb from λανθάνω; privately:--privily, secretly. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
a prolonged form of an otherwise obsolete verb; to talk, i.e. utter words:--preach, say, speak (after), talk, tell, utter. Compare λέγω. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

a prolonged form of a primary verb, which is use only as an alternate in certain tenses; to take (in very many applications, literally and figuratively (properly objective or active, to get hold of; whereas δέχομαι is rather subjective or passive, to have offered to one; while αἱρέομαι is more violent, to seize or remove)):--accept, + be amazed, assay, attain, bring, X when I call, catch, come on (X unto), + forget, have, hold, obtain, receive (X after), take (away, up). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
apparently a primary word; a people (in general; thus differing from δῆμος, which denotes one's own populace):--people. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

a primary verb; properly, to "lay" forth, i.e. (figuratively) relate (in words (usually of systematic or set discourse; whereas ἔπω and φημί generally refer to an individual expression or speech respectively; while ῥέω is properly to break silence merely, and λαλέω means an extended or random harangue)); by implication, to mean:--ask, bid, boast, call, describe, give out, name, put forth, say(-ing, on), shew, speak, tell, utter. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

from λέγω; something said (including the thought); by implication, a topic (subject of discourse), also reasoning (the mental faculty) or motive; by extension, a computation; specially, (with the article in John) the Divine Expression (i.e. Christ):--account, cause, communication, X concerning, doctrine, fame, X have to do, intent, matter, mouth, preaching, question, reason, + reckon, remove, say(-ing), shew, X speaker, speech, talk, thing, + none of these things move me, tidings, treatise, utterance, word, work. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
of Hebrew origin (מִרְיָם); Maria or Mariam (i.e. Mirjam), the name of six Christian females:-- Mary. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

from μάρτυς; to be a witness, i.e. testify (literally or figuratively):--charge, give (evidence), bear record, have (obtain, of) good (honest) report, be well reported of, testify, give (have) testimony, (be, bear, give, obtain) witness. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

of uncertain affinity; a witness (literally (judicially) or figuratively (genitive case)); by analogy, a "martyr":-- martyr, record, witness. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

(including the prolonged forms, feminine , plural , etc.; compare also μέγιστος, μείζων); big (literally or figuratively, in a very wide application):--(+ fear) exceedingly, great(-est), high, large, loud, mighty, + (be) sore (afraid), strong, X to years. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
of Hebrew origin (מַלְכִּי־צֶדֶק); Melchisedek (i.e. Malkitsedek), a patriarch:--Melchisedec. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

from  (probably derived from ἄγω; compare ἀγέλη) (to bring tidings); a messenger; especially an "angel"; by implication, a pastor:--angel, messenger. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from μετά and ἔχω; to share or participate; by implication, belong to, eat (or drink):--be partaker, pertain, take part, use. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

a primary particle of qualified negation (whereas οὐ expresses an absolute denial); (adverb) not, (conjunction) lest; also (as an interrogative implying a negative answer (whereas οὐ expects an affirmative one)) whether:--any but (that), X forbear, + God forbid, + lack, lest, neither, never, no (X wise in), none, nor, (can-)not, nothing, that not, un(-taken), without. Often used in compounds in substantially the same relations. See also ἐὰν μή, ἵνα μή, οὐ μή, μῆκος, μηκύνω, μήν, μὴ οὐκ. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
apparently a primary word; a "mother" (literally or figuratively, immediate or remote):--mother. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from a derivative of μνάομαι; to give a souvenir (engagement present), i.e. betroth:--espouse. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
of Hebrew  origin; (מֹשֶׁה); Moseus, Moses, or Mouses (i.e. Mosheh), the Hebrew lawgiver:--Moses. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
of Hebrew origin (נְתַנְאֵל); Nathanaël (i.e. Nathanel), an Israelite and Christian:--Nathanael. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

from a primary  (to parcel out, especially food or grazing to animals); law (through the idea of prescriptive usage), genitive case (regulation), specially, (of Moses (including the volume); also of the Gospel), or figuratively (a principle):--law. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
the definite article; the (sometimes to be supplied, at others omitted, in English idiom):--the, this, that, one, he, she, it, etc. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from ὀδύνη; to grieve:--sorrow, torment. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

from ὅς with the directive enclitic of source; from which place or source or cause (adverb or conjunction):--from thence, (from) whence, where(-by, -fore, -upon). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

of uncertain affinity; a dwelling (more or less extensive, literal or figurative); by implication, a family (more or less related, literally or figuratively):--home, house(-hold), temple. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

a prolonged form of a primary,                         but obsolete , for which                         another prolonged form            is used in certain tenses; to swear, i.e. take (or declare on) oath:--swear. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from ὅμοιος; to assimilate, i.e. compare; passively, to become similar:--be (make) like, (in the) liken(-ess), resemble. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
of uncertain derivation; a dream:--dream. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

from a presumed derivative of the base of γινώσκω (compare ὀνίνημι); a "name" (literally or figuratively) (authority, character):--called, (+ sur-)name(-d). [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

properly, to stare at (compare ὀπτάνομαι), i.e. (by implication) to discern clearly (physically or mentally); by extension, to attend to; by Hebraism, to experience; passively, to appear:--behold, perceive, see, take heed. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from  (a fence; perhaps akin to ὅριον); a limit, i.e. (sacred) restraint (specially, an oath):--oath. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

probably a primary word (or perhaps a form of the article ὁ); the relatively (sometimes demonstrative) pronoun, who, which, what, that:--one, (an-, the) other, some, that, what, which, who(-m, -se), etc. See also οὗ. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
of uncertain affinity; the loin (externally), i.e. the hip; internally (by extension) procreative power:--loin. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
from ὅς and τέ; at which (thing) too, i.e. when:--after (that), as soon as, that, when, while. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

neuter of ὅστις as conjunction; demonstrative, that (sometimes redundant); causative, because:--as concerning that, as though, because (that), for (that), how (that), (in) that, though, why. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

a primary word; the absolute negative (compare μή) adverb; no or not:--+ long, nay, neither, never, no (X man), none, (can-)not, + nothing, + special, un(-worthy), when, + without, + yet but. See also οὐ μή, μῆκος. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]

from οὐδέ and εἷς; not even one (man, woman or thing), i.e. none, nobody, nothing:--any (man), aught, man, neither any (thing), never (man), no (man), none (+ of these things), not (any, at all, -thing), nought. [source: MetaV Strongs.csv <- openscriptures/strongs CC BY-SA]
